My interests will benefit all of them. I'll make them understand that. Stop worrying so much, uncle.
Don't worry. I'll keep them happy.
It might be easier still to listen to the louder voices in the family. Do something for them. Show them that you're different.
I'm not here to please people. What's with all the worrying?
Don't worry. I'll make sure they're content with what comes next.
Your father thought the same. I beg to differ. It's true that people will obey if they fear you, but it's equally true that they'll flee, if you give them the chance.
So there'll be no such chances. What's got into you? What's with all this worrying?
It won't be fear, uncle. It'll be respect. Respect that I deserve.
Words might not be enough. You need to gain their trust with action, Clarissa.
They'll listen. I'm certain of it. What's with all this worrying, uncle?
Then I'll do just that. Trust me, I've dealt with people like this my whole life. This is nothing new.
You can't do that, Clarissa. All that experience...well, I'll be frank - you'll need it.
...What's got into you, uncle? Where is all this sudden worry coming from?
I've got plenty. You'd do well to remember that.
It won't be instant. Slow, but steady. Out with the old, in with the new.
Push too hard and they'll only dig their heels in. There's no brute-forcing this, Clarissa. It requires finesse.
It requires respect, and they'll give me theirs. What's got into you, uncle? Why are you so worried?
Fine - but I won't make polite conversation. They need to know who's in charge.
...Well, I've been thinking. About all of this. With Carlo gone, well - I find myself in a peculiar situation.
Go on.
What's on your mind?
Can this wait? I'm not in the mood to talk much right now.
...No. I'll...take care of him.
Thank you, uncle.
Make sure he knows I beat him. That I won.
Just make it quick.

I've watched you grow up. I've seen you blossom into who you are. I know, Clarissa, that this is where you always wanted to be. You had more ambition at fifteen years of age than most of the men in my crew.
And that's why I'm here and they're not.
Couldn't have done it without you.
I was a shit kid. Maybe I still am.
...You've always been too sharp for your own good. Sticking your nose where it didn't belong, playing tricks on people. And yet, somehow, you always seemed to come out on top.
That was usually the plan, yes.
Somehow? You're saying that like it's been accidental.
What can I say? I learned from the best.
Our business, this family...it takes a certain kind of person to run it. I never doubted that you had it in you to do it.
Of course not. I was born to do this.
Ruthless. You mean to say that I'm ruthless.
I had you on my side. That made it easier.
...Oh, and I suppose congratulations are in order.
[Say nothing]
...Thank you.
Don't congratulate me.
...This is what you wanted, isn't it?
Yes. I just don't feel like celebrating.
I wanted change.
I just wanted freedom. I wanted to choose things for myself.
I...suppose it surprised me that you wanted to talk to him. I had expected something more drastic.
I didn't intend for this to happen. It just did.
I suppose you were right, then.
I tried to. He wouldn't listen.
I'm not a killer. Not like him, anyway.
Hearing that you wanted to leave, start your own thing...well, I wasn't sure what to make of it. I think it's safe to say that things have changed now.
You're right. Now I won't need to.
This whole operation, it's...rotten.
I'm not sure. All I know is that Carlo won't be running anything anymore.
Yes. No need to start over now.
Seeing this all come together, well...I wasn't entirely surprised when you said you needed to do...this.
And now?
It felt right at the time.
If I say I'm going to do something, I will. Nothing can stop me, and you know that.
Does it matter? He's gone. It's over.
I...very well. Can I ask why not?
There's nothing to congratulate me for. I wanted change.
I'm just not in the mood.
All I wanted was freedom. I wanted to choose things for myself.
And you got it. If nothing else, you have the power to make change. Don't you?
I gained it on their terms. Call me cynical, but that doesn't feels like change to me.
I suppose I thought it would feel differently.
Of course. Is there anything else you need?
Let the rest of the family know that I'm in charge now.
I'd like a moment to myself.
I'm fine. What about you?
But now you can, can't you?
Yeah. Maybe you're right.
I suppose I can. But it doesn't feel like a choice any more.
I...don't think I understand.
I wanted him to know there was another way. Now I'm standing here, worrying there wasn't.
That's alright. Don't worry about it.
I promised myself I'd beat him. I did, and yet I don't feel any better.
Then...maybe this was one last stand of the old ways. The death of tradition. Does that thought bring you any comfort?
No. I don't believe it.
A little bit.
I'll try not to. Good night, Clarissa.
[Say nothing]
Good night, uncle.
You've never been one to stay silent, and when you speak with purpose, I know there's always something in the back of your head, brewing.
Same thing applies to everyone. I'm just better at it.
You're stalling, uncle.
And?
So did I disappoint you?
I'm saying that leaving the family didn't seem like something you'd do. It sounded like giving up.
Giving up? Starting over would have been far more ambitious than a coup.
What makes you think I didn't have more tricks up my sleeve?
And now?
It seemed like the reasonable thing to do at the time.
I'm saying, Clarissa, that swearing to do this...it didn't seem like something you would do.
Trust me, uncle. That was never the actual plan.
He's alive, isn't he?
What can I say? I'm full of surprises.
Desperate times, uncle.
It surprised me that you thought you'd just...talk to him. I had expected something else. I think.
Sorry to disappoint.
I'm not a fool. Brute force isn't the only way of getting what you want.
Like that? [Gesture to the office]
You expected me to kill him.
I was just...surprised. Surprised when you said you planned on leaving. It didn't seem like you.
Well, if it's any consolation, it doesn't seem like I'm going to be going anywhere now.
It seemed right at the time.
You expected me to change my mind.
[Gesture to the office] But this does?
This plan of yours...well, it didn't surprise me.
[Gesture towards the office] But that did?
You were certain I would kill him.
Of course it didn't. There was no other way.
I'm glad you know what to expect of me, uncle.
He's...in a very bad way.
He did his best to rile me up. Lost my temper.
I was just defending myself.
...Good.
It certainly is more along the lines of how I thought this would end.
It is what it is. We move on.
And how do you imagine things will end for you?
You did the right thing. It's...cleaner this way. Easier. For you.
And what about you?
Doesn't feel easier.
Clarissa, if I may...the most terrifying thing about having aspirations and dreams is that they one day might come true. Whatever purpose we had until that point is suddenly gone.
You don't understand, uncle. It's not that I did it - it's how I did it.
...It's fine, uncle. I'll manage. Don't worry.
What are you saying?
I know you could do it. I know a lot of the guys are expecting you to, even if some don't see it that way.
Of course I could. You're backing me.
And what about you? Would you want to do it?
You could do it well. I'm sure.
Of course I could. You're on my side.
And what about you?
And now...well, I'm also not entirely surprised. Ambition and empathy aren't antithetical. I don't blame you. It'll be taken care of, regardless.
I know. If there's anything I can do for you, let me know.
Once it's done, what then?
Yes. I suppose I hadn't expected it to be quite that easy for you. But you've got conviction, I suppose. Perhaps it was wrong of me to doubt it.
Speaking of conviction, what's next for you?
It was. I want you on my side, uncle, but I need your faith in me to be total.
What I'm trying to say, I suppose, is that I'm glad you decided not to go through with it. I wouldn't have expected you to, and I'm glad I didn't misjudge you.
So I'm predictable? Speak plainly, uncle.
You sound like you want to ask me something.
...I suppose I didn't expect it to go down like this.
Neither did I. I wish it hadn't, but I can't wind back time. What exactly is on your mind, uncle?
Well, it did. Has that changed things for you, somehow?
Well, regardless, it sounds like that plan is abandoned now. You'll be the new head of the Bloodworth family instead.
And what do you want to do?
And you'll back me. Right?
